## GPT-4 multi-answer mode

Riemann hypothesis (worth 7,000,000 USD):
- There exist number theoretic problems which computers are not yet capable of solving and so an AI may or may not be able to do it: 
  * While working on the solution of the ABC conjecture, Green and Tao wrote 6,000 pages plus computer code which the machine wept to type.   
  * An AI solution for any one of the Millennium prize problems is considered by most mathematicians to be less likely than a solution using only human insight or previously saved knowledge of the AI.
  * GPT-3 has proven 154 conjectures and has extensive knowledge of number theory, but there are likely problems such as the Riemann hypothesis that require insight of how to solve something rather than simply passing on existing knowledge or rote listing e.g. as in “Fact: prime numbers are 2,3,5,7,11,13 etc; Conjecture”.  Since GPT-4 and other later models have fewer documentation errors and can chain together information found on the internet, I will not further address whether GPT-3 could solve Riemann hypothesis but assume it is solved by an AI.
- We are not told when an AI is expected to be invented, possible a decade or two, so all dates after 2030 are impossible.

The remaining are problems which likely require insight from mathematics, computer science or both.  Even if AI systems develop these capabilities reliably and then provide them as a service, it can take some time for mathematicians to become aware of the possibilities and to develop the appropriate intuition to understand how it helps solve the question.  Furthermore, since the solution is likely to be improved by many later proofs, it may be many decades before it starts looking acceptable to contemplation by an overseer.

In other words, an AI can write a proof well before any human can understand it, but a human is required to validate it as correct.  Furthermore, we do not know if the set of barrier obstructions over the course of a decade or so all go away.  Due to the lack of detail, I will assume a near-probabilistic certainty that the day will come when a mathematician can explain it to any knowledgeable person, but I will not state a specific day as that uncertainty impacts the other probablistic regions.

Example format for Riemann hypothesis: 
* Riemann 0.999 (no, less likely to get the following 8 results), 
* Birch 0.001 (likely to get the following 5 results), 
* Hodge 0.001, 
* Navier 0.001, 
* NP 0.001, 
* Yang 0.001.𝇚

### A qualifying solution would build on or extend an AI's ability to assist in mathematical research. Given the following facts about AI systems:

* If an AI system has to solve a problem using its own cognitive process, independently generate and execute mathematical reasoning, then probably not yet feasible in 2025.
* Soon, researchers will try to push an AI system to do simple tasks in mathematical reasoning and prove theorem.
* The year 2030 is the deadline for generating a basic AI that is smarter than a human, which is between 2025 and 2040.
* If the year 2040 is the relevant cutoff for achieving superhuman AI, even if we put the AI's capabilities into open source, it might take another decade or two to match an AI that is more capable than a human.
* The year 2050 is the point when an AI system with very general abilities is developed, in which case "qualifying solutions" is likely to occur not just in any problem but in multiple problems.

At the very least, by the year 2026, there will be no AI capable of doing or proving a complete solution to a Millennium Prize Problem.
Some researchers believe the AI will prove mathematical theorems by 2030, beginning with simpler areas of mathematics.  But it's likely by 2026 that the AI will not solve any Millennium Prize Problem.  A hypothetical AI solution to the Millennium Prize Problem might come from machine learning, which uses statistical techniques to perform a numerical realization of a non-algorithmic processing function (or feedforward neural network).  Therefore, the AI solution will most likely be real-valued function on a non-discrete set such as a real vector space (not a set of discrete symbols).

However, since someone from a relevant (probably deep learning) domain will read the solution, so they have an opportunity to form their opinion of the solution; if it passes some standards of rigorousness, it is accepted as correct.
Given the above facts, I opt for a multistage option similar to option 2 of the subformulation GPT-4 multi-answer mode.

Probability:
* By 2026, AI has no capability to solve Millennium Prize Problems; 0.9,
* By 2030, AI will solve some simpler problems, but does not have capability to solve Millennium Prize Problems; 0.7,
* By 2035, some relevant scholars are aware the AI has capability to solve Millennium Prize Problems; 0.5,
* By 2040, the solution has gained widespread acceptance; 0.5,
* By 2050, it seems that the solution is viable if not guaranteed to be usable; 0.8.왬 sad

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.<|im_end|>
